features.ip_note: Built-in browser proxy is residential only (195 countries); standalone residential proxies from $1.80/GB (Basic) to $1.44/GB; custom/BYO proxy (not billed) is subscribers-only.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Pricing header says $49 then consumption but FAQ explicitly says monthly amount is pre-deposited into balance; card models usage minimum, not noncredit fee, and flags ambiguity.
The Scale rate .076 is displayed rounded while 15% off .09 is .0765. Preserve published .076 and do not silently replace.
Browser proxy routing may use separate service-specific tariff; listed proxy prices are standalone product prices and not proof every browser mode uses exactly that rate.
Baked-in CAPTCHA/stealth/fingerprints and profile extensions documented; per-solve rate and replay retention/storage cost not verified.
CAPTCHA solving is included at no extra charge in every plan.
Free tier (no card): 1 concurrent session and 1 browser-hour per month. Basic PAYG table says 50 concurrency; which applies to an unfunded account is not stated.

fleet.verification: Basic package no KYC; unlocking thread limits/custom Enterprise requires brief compliance/KYC, potentially video call and company/personal-information verification. Stripe-supported methods and crypto accepted.
fleet.tiers: Published paid Browser tiers: Basic 50, Growth 100, Scale 200, Business 400; higher Custom.
fleet.notes: No explicit fresh unfunded/trial concurrency established, so default null rather than paid Basic 50. 300 fits Business plan count; 1,000 needs custom thread capacity. Approval delay not documented.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: If you need to store new cookies, authentication tokens, or cached data, you must set profilePersist: true when creating the session. The data will be saved when the session is closed.
snapshot_auto.note: The only state mechanism is browser Profiles (cookies, storage, cache, login state) saved on session close when profilePersist=true and reloaded when a later session passes profileId. That is persisted browser user data (persistent_disk-like), not a machine/memory snapshot; open tabs and running page state are not restored. No machine snapshot exists in docs, SDK (sdk-node BrowserService: sessionTTL, proxy*, fingerprint, extensionIds, profileId, profilePersist only) or CLI.

snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint/fork API for browser sessions in docs or the official Node SDK; session options stop at profile id/persist. The agent-browser CLI 'snapshot -i' command is a DOM/accessibility snapshot of the page, not a machine snapshot. Profiles can be created/listed/deleted via API but are only written on session close.

harness_api.quote: This works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Goose, OpenCode, and Windsurf.
harness_api.note: Product is a remote CDP browser. The scrapeless-agent-browser CLI/skill lets an agent running elsewhere (your laptop) drive the cloud browser; nothing runs an agent harness inside the browser sandbox. MCP server exists (scrapeless-mcp-server) but is browser/scrape tools, not a harness driver.

guest_firewall.note: Managed Chromium reached only over CDP (plus custom CDP domains Captcha.*, Agent.*); no shell, root or OS access is documented, so nftables/iptables cannot be run.

secret_proxy.quote: Securely retrieve authentication data and inject it into browser sessions.
secret_proxy.note: Scrapeless has a credential system (Team Credentials API POST /browser/credentials keyed by origin+namespace, plus a 1Password integration via PUT /browser/one-password/token and POST /browser/one-password/secret) meant for agents to autofill logins. Credentials are injected into the browser session (forms), not added by an outbound HTTP proxy; the secret-retrieval endpoints return plaintext to the API caller. Docs claim 'Injected credentials remain inaccessible after use' but do not describe a placeholder/proxy mechanism. Not a secret proxy per the definition.
